its own multi-index, no two source elements can ever target the same output
cell, so the scatter is conflict free and can be expressed as a fused
"zero-fill + write selected cells" kernel.

The output is viewed as (outer, red, inner) with

    idx_ptr,
    out_ptr,

profile.summary: launch: Runtime is set by program (Block) count at ~0.5-0.7 us of scalar-pipe time per program, invariant to the work inside the program, Identical program count and element count at 2x bytes gives identical 0.61 ms - the bound is per-program, not per-byte, Masked-store element-wise predication is NOT the bottleneck (hypothesis b contradicted)

conclusion.root_cause: Baseline architecture (single fused zero-fill + selected-write launch, one program per contiguous `red` row for the inner==1 fast path, masked store) is numerically exact on all 96 workloads (abs_err=0 on every correctness case), confirming the conflict-free scatter analysis and the flat-element stride addressing. Performance is program-count bound rather than bandwidth bound: profile evidence on round 1 shows a flat ~0.62 us scalar-pipe cost per program (aiv_scalar_ratio 0.68-0.88, aiv_vec_ratio only 0.043-0.099) while work per program spans 128-4096 elements, so kernel time ~= BlockNum * 0.62us / 20 cores. The worst workloads launch 32768 programs of only 1KB each (timing-5/11/17 at 0.13x), and fp16 vs fp32 8192^2 take identical time despite 2x the bytes, which rules out a per-byte store bound.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Baseline geo_mean 0.6851 with min_speedup 0.1277 (worst: timing-5, 128x256x512 dim2, 32768 programs). Small shapes already beat the reference (timing-0/3/6/9/12/15 at 1.48-1.58x) because one launch replaces the reference zeros+scatter_ pair; large-outer shapes lose 2-8x because the per-program cost dominates. Comparing the two competing explanations from the profile: masked-store predication is contradicted (vector share is flat at 4-10% for every BLOCK and per-program scalar cost is flat-to-falling as BLOCK grows 32x), UB pressure is contradicted (tiles are 0.25-8KB against 192KB UB, no spills), so the gap is explained by too many tiny programs. Element-per-program must rise by roughly 8-32x, with all timing shapes having a power-of-two `red` so an unmasked store is available.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Replace the one-row-per-program fast path with a 2D [ROWS, COLS] tile kernel that owns ROWS consecutive outer rows: val = where(cols[None,:] == idx[:,None], g[:,None], 0), grid = ceil(outer/ROWS), ROWS = pow2(TILE//red) capped at 64 with TILE=8192, using the unmasked store when COLS==red and ROWS divides outer. That cuts timing-5 from 32768 to 2048 programs and should move the large-outer workloads toward the ~400GB/s store bound while keeping all correctness cases exact.
conclusion.debug_lesson: Per-workload latency that tracks element count instead of byte count is the signature of a launch/program-count bound on Ascend, not a bandwidth bound; verify with per-program cost and vector-ratio counters before changing tile bytes.

plan.strategy: Amortize the flat per-program launch/dispatch cost by giving each program ROWS consecutive outer rows (multi-row 2D tile with one contiguous store per program).
plan.code_changes: Replaced the one-row-per-program inner==1 fast path with a 2D [ROWS, COLS] tile kernel: grid = ceil(outer/ROWS), each program owns ROWS consecutive contiguous output rows, loads ROWS contiguous grad/indices values, builds val = where(cols[None,:] == idx[:,None], g[:,None], 0) and stores a contiguous ROWS*COLS block. ROWS = pow2(8192//red) capped at 64 and at outer; the store is unmasked when COLS==red and ROWS divides outer. inner>1 path unchanged.
plan.hypothesis: Round-1 profile showed a flat per-program cost of ~0.5-0.7us with aiv_scalar_ratio 0.68-0.88 and aiv_vec_ratio only 0.04-0.10, so kernel time is proportional to program count rather than bytes (fp16 and fp32 8192^2 both take ~0.62ms). Packing ROWS rows into one program with one contiguous store per program should cut the program count 2-16x and lift geo_mean above 1.0.

expected_effect.mechanism: Fewer, larger programs amortize the flat ~0.62us per-program scalar cost: timing-5/11/17 fall from 32768 to 2048 programs, timing-4/10/16 to 256, timing-2/8/14 from 16384 to 8192, so large-outer shapes approach the store-bandwidth bound while staying above the 20-core parallelism floor.

import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def _vsrb_lastdim_kernel(
    grad_ptr,
    idx_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    outer,
    red,
    g_s0,
    i_s0,
    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
    COLS: tl.constexpr,
    MASKED: tl.constexpr,
):
    """inner == 1 fast path: ROWS consecutive (contiguous) output rows per program."""
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    rows = pid * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
    cols = tl.arange(0, COLS)
    if MASKED:
        rmask = rows < outer
        g = tl.load(grad_ptr + rows * g_s0, mask=rmask, other=0.0)
        idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + rows * i_s0, mask=rmask, other=-1).to(tl.int32)
    else:
        g = tl.load(grad_ptr + rows * g_s0)
        idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + rows * i_s0).to(tl.int32)
    val = tl.where(
        cols[None, :] == idx[:, None],
        g[:, None],
        tl.zeros([ROWS, COLS], dtype=g.dtype),
    )
    offs = rows[:, None] * red + cols[None, :]
    if MASKED:
        tl.store(
            out_ptr + offs,
            val,
            mask=rmask[:, None] & (cols[None, :] < red),
        )
    else:
        tl.store(out_ptr + offs, val)


@triton.jit
def _vsrb_general_kernel(
    grad_ptr,
    idx_ptr,
    out_ptr,
    red,
    inner,
    g_s0,
    g_s1,
    i_s0,
    i_s1,
    IB: tl.constexpr,
):
    """inner > 1: one (outer, inner-block) tile per program."""
    o = tl.program_id(0)
    ib = tl.program_id(1)
    i = ib * IB + tl.arange(0, IB)
    mask = i < inner
    g = tl.load(grad_ptr + o * g_s0 + i * g_s1, mask=mask, other=0.0)
    idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + o * i_s0 + i * i_s1, mask=mask, other=-1).to(tl.int32)
    base = (o * red) * inner
    z = tl.zeros([IB], dtype=g.dtype)
    for r in range(red):
        v = tl.where(idx == r, g, z)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + r * inner + i, v, mask=mask)

    while b * 2 <= x and b * 2 <= cap:
        b *= 2
    return b

    ndim = len(shape)
    d = int(dim)
    if d < 0:
        d += ndim

    outer = 1
    for s in shape[:d]:
        outer *= s
    red = shape[d]
    inner = 1
    for s in shape[d + 1:]:
        inner *= s

    g_s1 = grad.stride(-1) if grad.dim() > 0 else 0
    i_s1 = indices.stride(-1) if indices.dim() > 0 else 0
    g_s0 = g_s1 * inner
    i_s0 = i_s1 * inner

    if inner == 1 and red <= 8192:
        # One program owns ROWS consecutive (contiguous) output rows: fewer,
        # larger programs amortize the flat per-program cost measured on the
        # target, and the store covers a contiguous ROWS*red element block.
        COLS = _pow2_at_most(red, 8192)
        TILE = 8192
        rows_cap = 64
        ROWS = _pow2_at_most(max(TILE // red, 1), rows_cap)
        if ROWS > outer:
            ROWS = _pow2_at_most(outer, rows_cap)
        nblk = (outer + ROWS - 1) // ROWS
        MASKED = (COLS != red) or (outer % ROWS != 0)
        _vsrb_lastdim_kernel[(nblk,)](
            grad,
            indices,
            out,
            outer,
            red,
            g_s0,
            i_s0,
            ROWS=ROWS,
            COLS=COLS,
            MASKED=MASKED,
        )
    else:
        IB = _pow2_at_most(inner, 1024)
        nblk = (inner + IB - 1) // IB
        _vsrb_general_kernel[(outer, nblk)](
            grad, indices, out, red, inner, g_s0, g_s1, i_s0, i_s1, IB=IB
        )
    return out

conclusion.root_cause: The multi-row tile kernel achieved its program-count goal (32768->2048 programs on timing-5, large-outer shapes now 1.02-1.42x) but the wrapper computed COLS with a round-down power-of-two helper, so any non-power-of-two `red` (only the [2,3,5] correctness cases, red=5) dropped the last columns and produced 6 INCORRECT_NUMERICAL results; the 8192^2 shapes remain element-rate limited independent of program count.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Predicted program-count reduction was observed on the large-outer shapes: timing-5 1.227->0.152ms (0.13x->1.02x, 32768->2048 programs), timing-4 0.309->0.114ms (0.51x->1.36x), timing-16 0.302->0.106ms, timing-10 0.309->0.114ms, timing-11 1.222->0.152ms; small shapes stayed 1.34-1.42x and timing-1/7/13 ~1.0x. Two deviations from the expectation: (1) 6 of 78 correctness cases FAILED (fp16/bf16/fp32 sizes [2,3,5] dim=2 keepdim both) because COLS was computed as the largest power of two <= red, so red=5 produced COLS=4 and the tail column was never written - matched_ratio 0.83-0.93 with the missing cells left at zero; (2) timing-2/8 (8192^2 fp16/bf16) only moved 0.624->0.603ms despite halving 16384->8192 programs, showing that shape is not program-count bound: it and fp32 8192^2 both sit at ~111 Melem/s (212 GB/s fp16 vs 424 GB/s fp32), an element-rate limit distinct from the reference's byte-rate memset, so the tile kernel's per-element select/store path is the next bottleneck.
conclusion.next_suggestion: Repair COLS to next_pow2(red) (8 for red=5) and ROWS from TILE//COLS, then attack the remaining element-rate limit: 8192^2 fp16 (0.603ms, 0.51x) and fp32 (0.603ms) both run at ~111 Melem/s regardless of dtype, i.e. an element-rate bound rather than the reference's ~420 GB/s byte-rate memset. Test a two-store program (wide contiguous constant zero store + patch scatter of the ROWS selected cells) in a bounded target debug microbenchmark before spending an eval round on it.
conclusion.debug_lesson: A power-of-two tile extent must be the NEXT power of two >= the logical extent; reusing a block-size helper that rounds down silently drops the tail columns and only fails on non-power-of-two extents (red=5 here).
